proposed_comments.title: Preserve provider identity in recent-command history
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The safe fix coordinates history schema, resolution, scoring, context-menu removal, migration, and tests across multiple files.
proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve provider identity in recent-command history

**Severity:** `high`

**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels/HistoryItem.cs`, `RecentCommandsManager.cs`, `TopLevelCommandResolver.cs`, `Commands/MainListPage.cs`, `Commands/RecentCommandListItem.cs`, and `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/CommandPaletteContextMenuFactory.cs`.

**Problem:** Recent history is keyed only by `CommandId`. When two providers, or a provider command and an All Apps item, expose the same id, the recent section, frecency score, and remove command can select or delete the wrong entry.

**Why it matters:** Users can invoke one command and later see another provider's command promoted, or remove one recent item and unexpectedly remove every entry sharing its id.

**Suggested change:**
1. Persist optional provider identity with each history item and introduce a `(ProviderId, CommandId)` identity with legacy id-only support.
2. Index, enumerate, score, and remove history by that identity.
3. Pass provider ids from top-level and All Apps call sites.
4. Prefer exact provider/id resolution and migrate legacy entries when next recorded.
5. Add collision, migration, scoring, and provider-specific removal tests.

**Verification:** Run the CmdPal ViewModels suite and verify the two-provider collision and legacy migration scenarios; the converged candidate passes 361/361 tests.

confidence.rationale: The current code resolves colliding ids without provider identity; the fork correction and regressions pass.

proposed_comments.title: Keep pinned commands and Alt shortcuts stable when Recent appears first
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The correction spans resolver ownership, shelf shortcut indexing, user-facing resource text, and tests.
proposed_comments.body:
### Keep pinned commands and Alt shortcuts stable when Recent appears first

**Severity:** `medium`

**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels/TopLevelCommandResolver.cs`, `QuickAccessShelfResolver.cs`, and `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Strings/en-us/Resources.resw`.

**Problem:** Resolving recent commands before pinned commands when `recentCommandsFirst` is true lets Recent consume commands that should remain owned by Pinned, while shelf shortcut indexes are assigned from presentation order.

**Why it matters:** Reordering sections can displace pinned items or make familiar Alt+number shortcuts launch recent commands instead.

**Suggested change:**
1. Resolve and reserve pinned ownership before resolving recent commands.
2. Apply visual section order only after ownership is established.
3. Assign pinned shortcut indexes from pinned order and recent indexes after the pinned range.
4. Document the stable shortcut behavior.
5. Add recent-before-pinned, pinned-limit, and shortcut-index tests.

**Verification:** Run the CmdPal UI build and ViewModels suite; the converged candidate passes 361/361 tests.

confidence.rationale: Presentation order currently determines ownership and shortcut numbering; the fork separates those concerns.

proposed_comments.title: Cap quick-access shelf recent items at five
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The safe correction requires a shared normalization helper, call-site update, resource text, and tests.
proposed_comments.body:
### Cap quick-access shelf recent items at five

**Severity:** `medium`

**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels/QuickAccessShelfViewModel.cs`, `QuickAccessShelfResolver.cs`, and the recent-command limit description in `Resources.resw`.

**Problem:** The Home setting allows up to 10 recent commands, and the compact shelf applies that same maximum despite the intended five-item shelf behavior.

**Why it matters:** Ten recent shelf items can overfill the compact row and create misleading expectations for visible Alt shortcuts.

**Suggested change:**
1. Add a shelf-specific maximum of five and normalize shelf configuration through it.
2. Keep the Home setting's existing 1-10 range.
3. Update the setting description to distinguish Home and shelf limits.
4. Add shelf limit tests for 1, 5, and values above 5.

**Verification:** Run the CmdPal UI build and ViewModels suite; the converged candidate passes 361/361 tests.

confidence.rationale: The current shelf directly reuses the broader Home maximum; the fork enforces the documented compact limit.

proposed_comments.title: Normalize invalid persisted recent-placement values
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: This requires a model-boundary normalization change plus serialization regression coverage.
proposed_comments.body:
### Normalize invalid persisted recent-placement values

**Severity:** `medium`

**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels/SettingsModel.cs` and `src/modules/cmdpal/Tests/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels.UnitTests/SettingsServiceTests.cs`.

**Problem:** `RecentCommandsOnQuickAccessShelf` and `RecentCommandsOnHome` deserialize arbitrary integers directly into enum auto-properties, allowing invalid persisted enum state into the model.

**Why it matters:** Behavior then depends on every consumer defensively handling unknown values instead of enforcing a valid settings invariant once.

**Suggested change:**
1. Back both properties with fields.
2. Retain only `BeforePinned` and `AfterPinned`; normalize all other values to `Hidden`.
3. Add serialization tests for invalid values such as `-1` and `99`.

**Verification:** Run `SettingsServiceTests` and the complete ViewModels suite; the converged candidate passes 361/361 tests.

confidence.rationale: Deserialization currently accepts undefined enum integers; model-level normalization removes that invalid state.
